bug_semantics: Query Builder deleteBatch() compiled prior where() conditions by replacing each named placeholder with bind[0] directly. Because the accompanying bind escape flag in bind[1] was ignored, a user-controlled string such as nobody' OR 1=1 -- was inserted into the DELETE SQL without quoting or escaping and could turn the WHERE value into executable SQL; ordinary delete() did not use this vulnerable batch-only substitution path.
flaw_origin: Commit ec2dc8b43e78375d354f83d2f0b7950144b943bf first added BaseBuilder::deleteBatch() and _deleteBatch(), including the exact nested loop whose str_replace() inserted bind[0] into QBWhere conditions without consulting bind[1]. Its immediate parent 672e1548ddbd98ce07a81832d510f61dd245d3b6 has no deleteBatch symbol or vulnerable block. The public PR #6734 merge 2477f08627fb02f69d69c1b0174937905c56e3bb preserves ec2dc8b43e78375d354f83d2f0b7950144b943bf as the atomic first member rather than collapsing it into the merge.
ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object names human author and committer sclubricants <vaughnb@scoil.com>; its message is only 'Add deleteBatch() and _deleteBatch()' and contains no Co-authored-by, Generated-with, AI-assistance, or bot trailer/identity.
evidence: GitHub advisory GHSA-c9w5-rwh3-7pm9 and the published CVE.org record CVE-2026-63221 both describe the batch-only SQL injection: deleteBatch() with where() substituted bound values while ignoring escape flags; affected versions are >=4.3.0,<4.7.4 and the fixed version is 4.7.4.

git show ec2dc8b43e78375d354f83d2f0b7950144b943bf -- system/Database/BaseBuilder.php shows this one-parent commit adding deleteBatch(), _deleteBatch(), and str_replace(':' . $field . ':', $bind[0], $where['condition']) in the initial 96-line implementation.

git rev-list --parents -n 1 ec2dc8b43e78375d354f83d2f0b7950144b943bf returns only parent 672e1548ddbd98ce07a81832d510f61dd245d3b6; git grep deleteBatch 672e1548ddbd98ce07a81832d510f61dd245d3b6 -- system/Database/BaseBuilder.php returns no match, directly proving parent-tree absence.

git blame f5e463b9a3e986389ce285963e51a7f1fab6559f^ -L 2953,2958 -- system/Database/BaseBuilder.php attributes the complete vulnerable bind-substitution loop, including raw bind[0], to ec2dc8b43e78375d354f83d2f0b7950144b943bf.

git show 2477f08627fb02f69d69c1b0174937905c56e3bb and git rev-list 2477f08627fb02f69d69c1b0174937905c56e3bb^1..2477f08627fb02f69d69c1b0174937905c56e3bb^2 identify PR #6734 as a two-parent merge and preserve ec2dc8b43e78375d354f83d2f0b7950144b943bf as its first atomic member, so the merge is not used as the BIC.

git cat-file commit ec2dc8b43e78375d354f83d2f0b7950144b943bf shows author and committer sclubricants <vaughnb@scoil.com>, a GPG signature, the single-line subject, and no co-author, generated-with, AI, or bot marker.
git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms ec2dc8b43e78375d354f83d2f0b7950144b943bf is contained by v4.3.0 but not v4.2.12, matching the advisory's 4.3.0 affected boundary.

The advisory's direct fix f5e463b9a3e986389ce285963e51a7f1fab6559f replaces all raw batch WHERE substitutions in BaseBuilder, OCI8, and Postgre builders with convertWhereBindsForBatch(), which obeys bind[1], calls db->escape(), handles arrays, and substitutes via strtr; added tests exercise quoted injection strings and verify rows are not deleted.

git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms f5e463b9a3e986389ce285963e51a7f1fab6559f is contained by v4.7.4 but not v4.7.3; GitHub's release/advisory and CVE.org likewise name 4.7.4 as the patched boundary.
reasoning: The vulnerable lifecycle begins in ec2dc8b43e78375d354f83d2f0b7950144b943bf, not in the later PR merge: that atomic member creates the batch-delete path and directly writes the unsafe raw bind[0] substitution, while its verified immediate parent lacks the entire method. The flaw survives into the first affected tag v4.3.0. The cited direct fix f5e463b9a3e986389ce285963e51a7f1fab6559f changes precisely that source-to-sink conversion so escape-enabled WHERE binds are quoted before SQL assembly and adds injection regression coverage; its membership begins at the patched tag v4.7.4. Finally, the BIC commit object has a human author/committer and no AI marker, regardless of any later repository AI signal or the fix's authorship, so the real vulnerability is NOT_AI.
